item.title: US withdraws bombers from UK base amid suspected Iran-backed terror plot
item.description: The US has withdrawn all bombers from RAF Fairford in England after commanders received new threats about a suspected Iran-backed plot targeting the base.

item.title: Suspect eliminated attempting to infiltrate IDF post in southern Syria Security Zone
item.description: A short while ago, IDF soldiers identified a suspect attempting to infiltrate an IDF post in the Security Zone in southern Syria. Following a quick identification, the soldiers fired toward the suspect and eliminated him. No IDF injuries were reported.

item.title: Watch: ‘Zionism is racism’ resolution torn to shreds outside UK Parliament
item.description: WZO delegation head Matan Bar Noy tore up the Green Party resolution outside Parliament, invoking Chaim Herzog’s 1975 protest against the UN’s 'Zionism is racism' vote.

item.title: 'They won't break me': Yehuda Glick banned from Temple Mount for six months
item.description: Police issue six-month restraining order against Temple Mount activist Yehuda Glick, banning him from holy site. Claims it was due to prayers for wounded reservist.

item.title: Security failures exposed after Flydubai incident
item.description: An NSC probe will examine a series of warnings, missed intelligence and unresolved responsibility questions that allowed the hijacker to fly to Israel.

item.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu to public televised debate: 'Let the public decide'
item.description:
Yashar! Chairman Gadi Eisenkot invited Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to a public televised debate to be broadcast live across all media channels.
Eisenkot called on Netanyahu to provide the public with direct answers regarding the events of October 7 and proposed that the debate format, moderators, and allocation of speaking time be determined by mutual agreement between the two sides.

item.title: Winter’s party falls below threshold for first time in Kan News poll
item.description: Amcha Yisrael falls below the threshold for the first time in a Kan News poll, leaving Eisenkot’s bloc with 52 seats to Netanyahu’s 51.

item.title: Ireland players snub Israeli team a second time
item.description: Ireland’s players lowered their heads during Hatikvah and refused the customary handshake as political tensions overshadowed their latest Nations League meeting with Israel.

item.title: Reports of explosions in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Explosions were heard this evening in the Strait of Hormuz area. According to initial reports, the explosions were apparently caused by missiles fired from Iran at ships passing through the strait.

item.title: The vacation from Jewish History is over for Americans
item.description: The erasure of Jews and treating them as villains cannot be ignored. The post-Oct. 7 surge of antisemitism is not a misunderstanding that will fade whether Netanyahu wins the election or not. Opinion.

item.title: Bursts of gunfire heard near conference attended by Jewish Ra'am candidate
item.description:
Bursts of gunfire were heard on Sunday evening near a conference in Rahat attended by Ra'am candidate Yoav Segalovitz, a former Deputy Minister of Public Security. The shooting occurred against the backdrop of a dispute between clans in the city.
Segalovitz said: "During the gathering, bursts of gunfire were heard very close to us, in the early evening hours. What is inconceivable is that here in the city, this has almost become routine."
